detailed_rationale:
ACC Ltd (subsidiary of Ambuja Cements, part of Adani Group) posted FY26 (year ended Mar-2026) consolidated revenue of Rs 25,962 cr with net profit of Rs 2,137 cr - a second consecutive year of PAT decline (FY25: Rs 2,402 cr; FY24: Rs 2,335 cr) despite revenue growth. Q4 FY26 alone showed revenue of Rs 7,146 cr (+17-18% YoY) on a record quarterly volume of 11.9 MnT (+8% YoY), but net profit crashed 68% YoY to Rs 238 cr (vs Rs 751 cr), which the company attributed to elevated fuel/diesel/power costs, packaging-bag supply constraints and rupee depreciation linked to the West Asia conflict - i.e. a cost pass-through lag, not demand destruction. [DATA, one-off flag: OPM has swung between ~9% and ~19% across the last several reported quarters, so the true normalized margin is a judgment call, not a clean number - INFERENCE].

Balance sheet is clean: near debt-free (net debt ~Rs 429 cr as of Mar-2026), ROE 10.9%, ROCE 11.2%. Trailing P/E is ~12.3x (P/B 1.22x), well below historical Indian cement-major multiples (UltraTech/pre-merger Ambuja often 20x+), but this reflects two ACC-specific overlays rather than a cheap-growth mispricing: (a) the FY26 earnings base is itself depressed by the Q4 cost one-off, and (b) ACC is mid-merger into parent Ambuja Cements. Ambuja's board approved amalgamation of ACC (and separately Orient Cement) on 22-Dec-2025, appointed date 1-Jan-2026, swap ratio 100 ACC shares : 328 Ambuja shares; exchanges (BSE/NSE) gave no-adverse-observation/no-objection on 4-Jun-2026, with the scheme required to reach NCLT within 6 months of that clearance; completion is guided for FY27. Until the scheme closes, ACC's standalone listing is being wound down - holders are effectively underwriting Ambuja's combined-entity value and merger execution/timeline risk, not ACC's standalone growth.

On governance: SEBI gave the Adani Group a clean chit on the Hindenburg allegations in Sept-2025 (no LODR/PFUTP violations found, 22 of 24 probes closed with no adverse finding). Separately and still unresolved as of this pass, the Nov-2024 US DOJ/SEC indictment of Gautam Adani and Sagar Adani (bribery allegations tied to solar-power contracts) remains an open matter in US courts - the group denies the charges; this is a group-level legal overhang, not ACC/cement-specific, and is flagged rather than treated as resolved either way [DATA, verified fresh this pass].
recommendation_rationale: No quant score exists yet for ACC, so the V1 default is Hold. My independent read does not clear the bar for an escalated Sell either: the balance sheet is clean, volumes are record-high, and the Q4 FY26 profit collapse reads as a cost/timing one-off rather than a structural impairment. But this is not a disguised Buy either - the stock is functionally in merger-arb wind-down (likely delisting into Ambuja within FY27), its cheap trailing multiple is not a clean value signal, and near-term standalone earnings visibility is poor. Hold = own if already held; no fresh conviction case to add.
summary: ACC delivered record cement volumes in Q4 FY26 but a 68% YoY profit decline on cost pass-through lag, against a balance sheet that remains almost debt-free; the stock is also mid-process on its board-approved amalgamation into parent Ambuja Cements (100:328 swap, appointed date 1-Jan-2026, NCLT process pending, completion targeted FY27), so its low trailing multiple reflects merger-arb overhang and a depressed earnings base as much as any standalone value opportunity.
positive_para: Record quarterly cement volumes (11.9 MnT, +8% YoY) signal resilient underlying demand; the balance sheet is near debt-free (~Rs 429 cr net debt) providing safety; FY26 revenue grew double digits; SEBI's Sept-2025 clean chit on the Hindenburg allegations removes one governance overhang at the group level; the pending merger into Ambuja gives ACC shareholders a defined conversion path (100:328 swap) into a larger, more efficient combined 'One Cement' platform targeting meaningful per-tonne synergies.
negative_para: Profitability quality is weak right now: FY26 PAT fell for a second straight year and Q4 FY26 PAT collapsed 68% YoY on fuel/power/packaging cost pressure and rupee depreciation; OPM has swung roughly 9%-19% quarter to quarter, making the earnings base hard to trust for a clean re-rating case; the low trailing P/E (~12x) is not a clean cheap-growth signal since it partly reflects the pending amalgamation (ACC's standalone listing is itself being extinguished, NCLT filing/approval still pending as of this pass, completion targeted only for FY27 - execution/timing risk in between); promoter is Adani Group, and separate from the resolved SEBI/Hindenburg matter, an unresolved Nov-2024 US DOJ/SEC bribery-related indictment against Gautam Adani/Sagar Adani remains open - a group-level legal/reputational overhang.
reverse_dcf_judgment: Fair, not cheap. At ~12.3x trailing P/E (P/B 1.22x) against an FY26 earnings base depressed by the Q4 cost one-off, the low multiple is explained by (1) a temporarily suppressed earnings base and (2) the merger overhang capping any re-rating - not by the market underestimating growth. Even if margins normalize toward the ~14-15% high end of the recent 9-19% OPM range and volume growth holds at high-single digits, that mainly justifies a re-rating AFTER the Ambuja merger executes and the combined entity's synergy case is tested, not a standalone ACC re-rating today.
